edbDesc: Brewster's angle (also known as the polarisation angle) is an angle of incidence at which light with a particular polarisation is perfectly transmitted through a transparent dielectric surface, with no reflection. When unpolarised light is incident at this angle, the light that is reflected from the surface is therefore perfectly polarised.
title: Brewster's Angle
pickWhy: Borderline: Judgment call: Brewster found the exact angle in 1815, but the effect, light reflected off glass or water being polarised, is Malus's 1808 discovery on the Polarized light card; I linked it there.
